questions.question_english: Do C-R equations are necessary and sufficient for a function to be analytic?
questions.question_hindi: Do C-R equations are necessary and sufficient for a function to be analytic?
questions.explanation_english: We have for f(z) = u(x, y) + iv(x, y) to be analytic on a region D⊆ℂu(x, y) & v(x, y) must have continuous first order partial derivatives throughout D and u(x, y) & v(x, y) must satisfy Cauchy-Riemann equations throughout region D. Therefore, Cauchy-Riemann equations are necessary for a function to be analytic but not sufficient.

questions.explanation_english: An upper triangular matrix is a square matrix whose all the entries below the main diagonal are zero. Whereas a row echelon matrix need not be a square matrix. Therefore, all upper triangular matrices are in echelon from but not all matrices in echelon form are upper triangular matrices.
